status_observed: 200 â€” obligation bucketed into "August 2026" (due 2026-09-07) for a bill paid 2026-07-10; document event_date reported as 2026-08-26
what_is_wrong: For a tax head configured liability_arises_on=PAYMENT_DATE, the obligation engine dates the withholding event from the server wall clock at the moment the payment row was inserted, not from the user-entered payment_date. It reads PurchaseBill.paid_at, and purchase_bills.py sets paid_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc) while storing the real payment_date only on the child payment row. Consequence: a back-dated payment lands in the wrong statutory period, gets the wrong deposit due date, and a genuinely overdue liability is reported as not-yet-due. Because every newly recorded payment gets today's timestamp, obligations for PAYMENT_DATE heads always land in the current period, so overview's overdue_remittances / due_within_7_days can effectively never fire in normal use. The same wrong event_date appears on GET /api/v1/compliance/obligations/by-document (period_label "August 2026", event_date 2026-08-26 for the same bill).

what_is_wrong: After a withholding certificate is voided, the credit row correctly reverts to certificate_id=null / status=AWAITING_CERTIFICATE, but it still carries the voided certificate's certificate_reference. The row is internally contradictory: it reports having no certificate while displaying one's reference. On the Credits screen a receipt that needs a fresh certificate chased from the customer will render with a certificate reference next to "Awaiting Certificate". The documented search filter ("Matches Invoice Number, Customer, Certificate Ref") also still matches the voided reference, so searching a voided certificate number surfaces a row that claims to have no certificate.
suspected_cause: app/services/credits_engine.py:94-96 clears cert_id on VOIDED but leaves the local `cert` bound, so line 119 `certificate_reference=cert.certificate_reference if cert else None` still emits the voided reference
